title: Colocate Notifications Near Orders
description:
**SITUATION:**

Last lab you taught Notification Service a **soft node preference** — prefer the notification pool when it has room, but still schedule elsewhere so SMS/email never sits Pending.

That helped capacity. It did **not** fix today’s incident.

**Friday lunch rush (peak traffic):**

Order volume spikes. Every new order immediately enqueues a confirmation SMS/email. Dashboards show Order Processor healthy, but notification **queue lag** climbs — customers get “order confirmed” minutes late.

Tracing shows the bottleneck is not CPU on the notification pool. It is **distance**: Notification Pods often land on a different worker than Order Processor. Order events hop across nodes (and sometimes AZs) before Notification can drain the queue. Under peak load that crosstalk adds up.

Ops asks for a different soft rule for this window:

> Prefer Notification Pods on the **same node as Order Processor** when possible — so the handoff stays local. If that node is full, still schedule somewhere else (do not hard-pin and risk Pending during the rush).

That is **pod affinity** (prefer near certain Pods), not node-label affinity (prefer a pool). Setup already runs bare `notification-service` (2 replicas) and `order-processor-deploy` (target for affinity). Your job is the soft colocation rule.

[DevSetu Blog — Where Pods Land: Selectors, Affinity, and Taints](/play/devops-engineer/kubernetes/read/scheduling-affinity-taints)

**YOUR TASK:**

1. Confirm Order Processor Pods are up (`app=order-processor`) — they are the affinity target.
2. **Update** `notification-service` with **preferred pod affinity** toward those Pods (same hostname / node when possible).
3. Verify Notification Pods are **Ready**.

**SPEC:**

- Deployment name: `notification-service` (do not rename)
- Replicas: keep **`2`**
- `affinity.podAffinity.preferredDuringSchedulingIgnoredDuringExecution`:
  - weight: `100`
  - topologyKey: `kubernetes.io/hostname`
  - labelSelector: `app=order-processor`
- Do **not** require hard pod affinity (no `requiredDuringScheduling…` for this lab)
- Ready: **2/2** Notification Pods Ready

**GOOD PRACTICES:**

- Manifest: `notification-podaffinity-l27.yaml`.
- Affinity targets **Pods** (`app=order-processor`), not node labels like `workload=notifications`.
- Keep this preference **soft** — peak traffic must not leave Notification Pending.
- Work only in your lab namespace (not `default`).

hints: Your namespace is in the lab chrome and in $LEARNER_NS — kubectl already defaults there.
This lab is podAffinity toward app=order-processor — not nodeAffinity for workload=notifications from L26.
Check kubectl get pods -l app=order-processor -o wide before and after.
Work only in your lab namespace (not default).
Read SPEC carefully, apply your YAML, then Submit.
problemStatement.solution:
# Solution — Colocate Notifications Near Orders

During peak order traffic, prefer Notification on the same node as Order Processor (`podAffinity`, soft) so confirmations do not lag across the fabric. Still schedule elsewhere if that node is full.

Docs: [DevSetu Blog — Where Pods Land: Selectors, Affinity, and Taints](/play/devops-engineer/kubernetes/read/scheduling-affinity-taints) · [Inter-pod affinity](https://kubernetes.io/docs/concepts/scheduling-eviction/assign-pod-node/#inter-pod-affinity-and-anti-affinity)

## Solution YAML

Save as `notification-podaffinity-l27.yaml`:

```yaml
apiVersion: apps/v1
kind: Deployment
metadata:
  name: notification-service
spec:
  replicas: 2
  selector:
    matchLabels:
      app: notification-service
  template:
    metadata:
      labels:
        app: notification-service
    spec:
      affinity:
        podAffinity:
          preferredDuringSchedulingIgnoredDuringExecution:
            - weight: 100
              podAffinityTerm:
                topologyKey: kubernetes.io/hostname
                labelSelector:
                  matchLabels:
                    app: order-processor
      containers:
        - name: notification-service
          image: devsetu/notification-service:v1.0
          ports:
            - containerPort: 8080
```

## Declarative

```bash
kubectl apply -f notification-podaffinity-l27.yaml
kubectl get deploy notification-service -o yaml | grep -A30 podAffinity
kubectl get pods -l 'app in (notification-service,order-processor)' -o wide
```

Wait until **2/2** Notification Pods are Ready, then **Submit**.
